profile.title: Systems Thinking, Systems Practice
profile.canonical_definition: Peter Checkland's account of the action-research programme from which Soft Systems Methodology developed, joining systems ideas to inquiry in ill-structured real-world situations.
profile.summary: Systems Thinking, Systems Practice records the action-research programme that produced SSM and keeps theory and practice in a recursive relation rather than treating application as a final implementation stage.
profile.why_it_matters: It is a primary route into why SSM was developed, what it was designed to avoid and how systems thinking changes when inquiry concerns people with different purposes and interpretations.
common_misreadings: the book supplies a fixed seven-step recipe
models are proposed designs of reality
profile.editorial_note: Developed from public primary, institutional and publisher sources. Open to correction, rival interpretation and stronger evidence.
